title: Spiral Matrix
prompt: Given an `m x n` matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order: starting at the top-left, moving right across the top row, down the right column, left across the bottom row, up the left column, and continuing this inward spiral until every element has been visited.

examples.explanation: Traverse the top row left-to-right, then the right column top-to-bottom, then the bottom row right-to-left, then the remaining left column bottom-to-top, then spiral into the center.
A single-row matrix spirals as a simple left-to-right traversal, since there are no further rows to descend into.

hints: Track four shrinking boundaries: top, bottom, left, and right rows/columns still unvisited.

Traverse the top boundary left-to-right, then the right boundary top-to-bottom, then (if rows remain) the bottom boundary right-to-left, then (if columns remain) the left boundary bottom-to-top, moving each boundary inward after its pass.
After each of the four passes, check whether top > bottom or left > right, and stop once the boundaries cross — this handles non-square matrices correctly.

solution.approach: Maintain four boundaries: top, bottom, left, and right, representing the current unvisited rectangle. Repeatedly traverse the top row left-to-right then push top down; traverse the right column top-to-bottom then pull right in; if top <= bottom, traverse the bottom row right-to-left then pull bottom up; if left <= right, traverse the left column bottom-to-top then push left in. After each of the four legs, re-check the boundary conditions since a leg can exhaust the remaining rows or columns partway through a non-square matrix. Repeat until the boundaries cross, having visited every element exactly once.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space excluding the output
